ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r5.claim: Every creature receives a form suited to its purpose and instinctive guidance for its needs, sustenance, reproduction, protection, and role in the wider order.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r5.anchor: guidance to their instincts in accordance with their needs

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r6.claim: Birdsong and the distinctive forms, colors, scents, and benefits of plants and fruits all point to their Creator, the true Lord.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r6.anchor: Who has inspired the nightingale to chant, the parrots to sing

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r7.claim: God guides creatures in their sustenance, reproduction, protection, and role in the order of the universe.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p41/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p41/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p41/r1.claim: Human beings are God's finest earthly creation, but their bodily powers, instincts, intellect, and achievements are gifts rather than self-generated potential.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p41/r1.anchor: Human beings are the best of God’s creation on this earth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p41/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p41/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p41/r2.claim: People's travel, scientific discovery, and mastery of nature result from God-given intellect; they should not become arrogant and challenge God's kingdom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p41/r2.anchor: all this is a product of

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p41/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p41/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p41/r3.claim: Moses's concise, gentle answer corners Pharaoh: only the being who created and guided can claim to be God; Pharaoh did neither, as 87:1–3 also states.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p41/r3.anchor: only that being can claim to be his God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p41/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p41/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p41/r4.claim: Human intellect and nature themselves provide conclusive testimony to truth, as 75:14–15 says, even though people make excuses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p41/r4.anchor: human intellect and nature are sufficient

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p41/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p41/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p41/r5.claim: God-given intellect enabled people to discover physical laws and reach new heights; this should not lead them to defy God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p41/r5.anchor: All these marvels are the result of God-given intellect

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r1.claim: Sending messengers and books to guide humanity is an additional divine blessing.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p42/r1.anchor: It is God’s further blessing that He has also sent His

ASAD-NOTES:20:49#n31/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:49#n31/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:49#n31/r1.claim: Although Arabic uses the past tense, the sentence describes creation as continuous and timeless, an unceasing present.
ASAD-NOTES:20:49#n31/r1.anchor: it is independent of the concept of time and denotes, as in so many other places in the Qur'an

ASAD-NOTES:20:49#n31/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:49#n31/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:49#n31/r2.claim: Khalq here includes both a thing's inner nature and the outward form in which that nature appears, explaining Asad's composite translation.
ASAD-NOTES:20:49#n31/r2.anchor: The term khalq signifies in this context not merely the inner nature of a created thing or being but also the outward form in which this nature manifests itself

ASAD-NOTES:20:49#n31/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:49#n31/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:49#n31/r3.claim: Asad traces the underlying idea to 87:2-3, among the earliest Qur'anic revelations.
ASAD-NOTES:20:49#n31/r3.anchor: The idea underlying the above sentence is expressed for the first time in 87:2-3

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r11.claim: When Pharaoh mockingly asked who their Lord was, Moses answered that God gives every creature its nature and form and then guides it, so all owe their existence to Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r11.anchor: Mûsâ O’nun evrendeki her şeyi özüyle ve biçimiyle var eden sonra da her varlığa yolunu yordamını gösteren Allah olduğunu söylemiş, böylece Firavun da dahil olmak üzere her şeyin varlığını O’na borçlu olduğuna dikkat çekmişti.

BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r1.claim: The plural our Lord includes Moses, Aaron, Pharaoh, and others; Moses describes God by His acts rather than naming Him so the act points to its agent.
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r1.anchor: ومنه يفهم أن ضمير الجمع في ربنا عام لموسى وهارون وفرعون وغيرهم ولم يقل ربنا الله بل وصفه بأفعاله ليستدل بالفعل على الفاعل

BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r2.claim: By pure mercy, God gives every creature its fitting form, with the properties and benefits suited to it.
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r2.anchor: من محض رحمته {أعطى كل شىء} من أنواع المخلوقات {خلقه} أي : صورته وشكله

BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r3.claim: God guides each creature toward what naturally or voluntarily issues from it and equips it for its created purpose; the sequence marks creation before the endowment of powers.
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r3.anchor: وهيأه لما خلق له ولما كان الخلق الذي هو عبارة عن تركيب الأجزاء وتسوية الأجسام متقدما على الهداية

BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r4.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r4.claim: Some spiritual masters say every creature has life and spirit, formally in humans, jinn, and angels and meaningfully in inanimate things and plants.
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r4.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : إن للمخلوقات كلها حياة وروحا إما صورية

BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r5.claim: Since every creature glorifies God, each is guided to know Him according to its intellect, spirit, and life.
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r5.anchor: فما من مخلوق إلا وقد هدى إلى معرفته تعالى بقدر عقله وروحه وحياته

BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r6.claim: The Najmiyya reading takes each creature's allotted creation as its preparedness for its purpose, and guidance as making that purpose easy.
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r6.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {أعطى كل شىء خلقه} استعدادا لما خلق له {ثم هدى}

BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r7.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r7.claim: The Prophet says people should act, since each person is eased toward the purpose for which they were created.
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r7.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : "اعملوا فكل ميسر لما خلق له"

BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r8.claim: The Najmiyya account says believers are created receptive to faith and guided to follow prophets, while disbelievers are disposed to rejection and defiance.
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r8.anchor: معناه أن الله تعالى خلق المؤمن مستعدا لقبول فيض الإيمان ثم هداه إلى قبول دعوة الأنبياء ومتابعتهم وخلق الكافر مستعدا

BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r9.speaker: المغربي
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r9.claim: Al-Maghribī's poem says one person is created for obedience and another for disobedience, and continues by assigning them to Mālik and Riḍwān.
BURSEVI:v5p303#2/r9.anchor: قال المغربي قدس سره : يكى را بهر طاعت خلق كردند يكى را بهر عصيان آفريدند

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p17#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p17#4/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p17#4/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says God gave each thing what would make it sound or beneficial, then guided it to that.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p17#4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة عن الحسن في قوله ﴿ أعطى كل شيء خلقه ﴾ قال أعطى كل شىء ما يصلحه ثم هداه لذلك

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p17#4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p17#4/r2.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p17#4/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī says God gave each male its female—man and woman, camel and she-camel—and guided them to one another.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p17#4/r2.anchor: عن الكلبي قال أعطى الرجل المرأة والجمل الناقة والذكر أعطاه الأنثى ثم هداه لذلك

QASHANI:20:48-51/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:48-51/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:48-51/r3.claim: God’s giving each thing its form and guiding it means guiding the self by proof: He gives each being suitable constitution, faculties, benefits, aims, and direction to attain them.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r7.claim: Moses answers Pharaoh alone, as only Moses was directly questioned, and describes God with an attribute Pharaoh cannot plausibly claim.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r7.anchor: واستبد موسى عليه السلام بجواب فرعون من حيث خصه بالسؤال والنداء معا ثم أعلمه من صفات الله تعالى بالصفة التي لا شرك لفرعون فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari praises the answer as concise, comprehensive, clear, and persuasive to a fair-minded seeker of truth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r8.anchor: ولله در هذا الجواب ما أخصره وما أجمعه وما أبينه لمن ألقى الذهن ونظر بعين الإنصاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r9.claim: God gives every created thing its fitting form and perfect measure, distinguishing human from animal form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r9.anchor: أعطى كل ما خلق خلقته وصورته على ما يناسبه من الإتقان لم يجعل خلق الإنسان في خلق البهائم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r10.speaker: مجاهد، عطية، ومقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r10.claim: Mujahid, Atiyya, and Muqatil say God gave each thing its form.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r11.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r11.claim: Al-Dahhak says God made each thing with a fitting benefit and guided it to that benefit, as each organ suits its function.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r11.anchor: وقال الضحاك خلقه من المنفعة المنوطة به المطابقة له ثم هدى أي يسر كل شيء لمنافعه ومرافقه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r12.speaker: القشيري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r12.claim: Al-Qushayri takes khalq as created faculties deposited in the limbs, with all created things as the first object and their creation as the second.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r12.anchor: قال القشيري: والخلق المخلوق لأن البطش والمشي والرؤية والنطق معان مخلوقة أودعها الله للأعضاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن جبير، والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r1.claim: They interpret the verse to mean that each living thing receives a mate of its kind, then guidance to mating, food, drink, and shelter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r1.anchor: فلم يزاوج منهما غير جنسه ثم هداه إلى منكحه ومطعمه ومشربه ومسكنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says God guided creatures to their mates, union, and marriage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه هداه إلى إلفه والاجتماع به والمناكحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say God gave each thing its well-being and guided it to what would improve it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة أعطى كل شيء صلاحه وهداه لما يصلحه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r4.claim: A syntactic reading makes creation the first object and all things the second: God gave His creatures everything they need and use.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r4.anchor: وقيل كل شيء هو المفعول الثاني لأعطى وخلقه المفعول الأول أي أعطى خليقته كل شيء يحتاجون إليه ويرتفقون به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r5.speaker: عبد الله، أناس من أصحاب رسول الله، أبو نهيك، ابن أبي إسحاق، الأعمش، الحسن، نصير، ابن نوح، وسلام
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r5.claim: They read khalaqahu as a past verb with an open lām; the second object is omitted, and every creature receives God's gift and guidance in using it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r5.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وأناس من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبو نهيك وابن أبي إسحاق والأعمش والحسن ونصير عن الكسائي وابن نوح عن قتيبة وسلام خلقه بفتح اللام فعلا ماضيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r6.claim: On this reading, God did not withhold bounty from any creature and taught it how to benefit from what it received; the omitted object may be inferred from context.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r6.anchor: أي كل شيء خلقه لم يخله من عطائه وإنعامه ثم هدى أي عرف كيف يرتفق بما أعطى وكيف يتوصل إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya construes the omitted gift as each creature's perfection or benefit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p340/r7.anchor: وقدره ابن عطية كماله أو مصلحته

QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r14.claim: Moses answers by pointing to God’s acts—giving each thing its created form and guidance—as evidence for God’s existence.
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r14.anchor: ليعلم أن الدليل على إثباته - سبحانه - ما دلت عليه أفعاله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r1.claim: Moses gives the answer because Pharaoh directed the question to him in particular.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r1.anchor: أي موسى عليه السلام واستبد بالجواب من حيث أنه خص بالسؤال

ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r2.claim: Grammatically, “our Lord” is the subject and the relative clause its predicate; alternatively, it is the predicate of an omitted “He is,” with the relative as modifier.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : هو خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي هو ربنا والموصول صفته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r3.claim: The first-person plural may mean Moses and Aaron, or, as some investigators argue, all creatures, answering Pharaoh by establishing the truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعض المحققين : اراد جميع المخلوقات تحقيقا للحق وردا عن اللعين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r4.claim: In the first parsing, “everything” is the first object and “its creation” the second; the latter is a passive participle, and its pronoun refers to “everything.”
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r4.anchor: مفعول أول لاعطى و ( خلقه ) مفعوله الثانى وهو مصدر بمعنى اسم المفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r5.claim: The universal applies to individuals: God gives each its dispositionally sought or fitting form, shape, benefit, and properties, as the eye and ear suit seeing and hearing.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r5.anchor: أي أعطى كل شئ من الأشياء الأمر الذي طلبه بلسان استعداده من الصورة والشكل والمنفعة والمضرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r6.claim: A proposed reading keeps “creation” as a verbal noun, meaning each thing receives the act of creating suited to its readiness or proper form; al-Alusi considers it weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r6.anchor: وقيل : الخلق باق على مصدريته بمعنى الايجاد أي أعطى كل شئ الايجاد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r7.claim: Some restrict “everything” to kinds rather than individuals, to avoid incomplete individuals caused by incidental defects.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r7.anchor: وحمل بعضهم العموم على عموم الأنواع دون عموم الأفراد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r8.claim: Al-Alusi rejects narrowing the scope: Sunni consensus holds God creates and commands through wisdom as grace, not obligation; each thing is complete in its rank, and creation shows no disparity.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r8.anchor: والحق أن الله تعالى راعى الحكمة فيما خلق وأمر تفضلا ورحمة لاوجوبا وهذا مما اجمع عليه أهل السنة والجماعة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r9.claim: The past tense is no reason to restrict the scope to kinds: although many individuals are yet to exist, kinds already exist and no new kind need arise; the proposed objection remains debatable.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r9.anchor: سبب العدول كون ( أعطى ) حقيقة فى الماضى فلو حمل كل شئ على عموم الأفراد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن جبير، السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r10.claim: They explain the phrase as each animal being given a female counterpart resembling it in form, treating “all” as indicating abundance.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r10.anchor: وروى عن ابن عباس وابن جبير والسدى أن المعنى أعطى كل حيوان ذكر نظيره فى الخلق والصورة انثى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r11.claim: Al-Alusi treats the animal-pairing interpretation as an example of the broader fitting-gift meaning, not a literal universal, and doubts that its named authorities intended the literal claim.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r11.anchor: وعندى أن هذا المعنى من فروع المعنى السابق الذى ذكرناه ولعل مراد من قاله التمثيل وإلا فهو بعيد جدا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r12.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r12.claim: Al-Jubba’i reverses the objects: “its creation” is first, while “everything” is second, meaning God gives creatures what they need; al-Alusi finds the usual parsing clearer in wording and meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200#2/r12.anchor: ونسب هذا القول إلى الجبائى والأول اظهر لفظا ومعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r1.speaker: عبد الله، وأناس من أصحاب رسول الله، وأبو نهيك، وابن أبي إسحاق، والأعمش، والحسن، ونصير، وابن نوح، وسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r1.claim: These authorities read “creation” as the active past verb “he created”; the clause modifies the preceding noun, with the second object elided as context supplies it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r1.anchor: وقرا عبد الله واناس من اصحاب رسول الله ( صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r2.claim: On that reading, God gave each created thing what repairs or benefits it, or what it needs.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r2.anchor: أي أعطى كل شئ خلقه تعالى ما يصلحه أو ما يحتاج اليه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari likens the construction to “gives and withholds”: God has not left any created thing without gift and favor; al-Kashf calls this clearer and more eloquent, while al-Alusi remains hesitant.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r3.anchor: وجعل ذلك الزمخشرى من باب يعطى ويمنع أي كل شئ خلقه سبحانه لم يخله من عطائه وانعامه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r4.claim: Al-Alusi considers the other grammatical analysis better crafted and more fitting to context, and closer to the first reading’s initial interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r4.anchor: الأول احسن صناعة وموافقه المقام وهو عندى أوفق بالمعنى الأول للقراءة الأولى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r5.claim: “Then he guided” means God directed and showed the way; these created things point to their maker, whose existence, wisdom, and generosity they demonstrate.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r5.anchor: أي ارشد ودل سبحانه بذلك على وجوده وجوده فان من نظر في هذه المحدثات

ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r6.claim: “Then” marks rank, not elapsed time: guidance follows creation in ontological order, though no time separates them.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r6.anchor: وهذا الجعل وان كان متأخر بالذات عن الخلق وليس بينهما تراخ في الزمان اصلا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r7.speaker: إرشاد العقل السليم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r7.claim: Al-Irshad explains guidance as teaching each creature how to benefit from its gifts and attain preservation and perfection, by choice in animals and natural powers in other beings.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r7.anchor: طريق الانتفاع والارتفاق بما اعطاه وعرفه كيف يتوصل إلى بقائه وكماله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r8.claim: Al-Alusi objects that creation is linguistically broader than bodily assembly and already includes moving and perceiving powers; this interpretation also makes “guided” metaphorical.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r8.anchor: الخلق لغة اعم مما ذكره وان القوى المحركة والمدركة داخلة فى عموم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r9.speaker: ابن عباس ومن معه
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r9.claim: A transmitted interpretation says God guided creatures to union through affinity and mating; other interpretations are also mentioned without detail.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r9.anchor: على التفسير المروى عن ابن عباس ومن معه ثم هداه إلى الاجتماع بالفة والمناكحة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r10.claim: Al-Alusi praises the answer as concise, comprehensive, and clear to a fair seeker; instead of the obvious title “Lord of the worlds,” Moses points to the origination, dependence, and differing ranks of all beings.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p201/r10.anchor: سلك طريق الارشاد والاسلوب الحكيم واشار إلى حدوث الموجودات باسرها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r1.claim: Some infer Pharaoh knew God but rebelled: the relative clause had to be known to him, and its claim about creation would identify its Lord.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r1.anchor: استدل بالاية على أن فرعون كان عارفا بالله تعالى إلا أنه كان معاندا لأن جملة الصلة لا بد أن تكون معلومة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r2.claim: The argument also cites Pharaoh’s acknowledgment that Moses’ signs came from the Lord of the heavens and earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r2.anchor: لقد علمت ما انزل هؤلاء إلا رب السموات والأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r3.claim: They cite the statement that the opponents inwardly knew the signs were true but denied them unjustly and arrogantly.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r3.anchor: وجحدوا بها واستيقنتها أنفسهم ظلما وعلوا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r4.claim: They cite the account that Pharaoh and his people thought they would not return to God, construing this as denial of resurrection rather than of the Creator.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى في سورة القصص : ( وظنوا أنهم الينا لا يرجعون ) فانه ليس فيه إلا انكار المعاد دون المبدا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r5.claim: They read Pharaoh’s “Who is the Lord of the worlds?” as asking for God’s essence, while his description of Moses’ Lord as a madman implies acknowledgment of existence.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r5.anchor: ان رسولكم الذى ارسل اليكم لمجنون

ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r6.claim: They argue Pharaoh was rational and so knew he arose after nonexistence and needed a governor; his limited realm also undercuts belief that he created the whole world.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r6.anchor: وكل عاقل يعلم بالضرورة أنه وجد بعد العدم ومن كان كذلك افتقر إلى مدبر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r7.claim: Al-Alusi says the question “who?” apparently followed a proof of existence; Moses then moved to the harder issue of divine essence, which humans cannot know, though these arguments are disputable.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r7.anchor: والظاهر أن السؤال بمن سابق فكان موسى عليه السلام لما أقام الدلالة على الوجود ترك المنازعة معه في هذا المقام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r8.speaker: من الناس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r8.claim: Others hold Pharaoh ignorant of God; proposed forms include denying any maker, necessary-cause philosophy, star or idol worship, indwelling, and anthropomorphism.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r8.anchor: ومن الناس من قال : أنه كان جاهلا بالله تعالى بعد اتفاقهم على

ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r9.claim: Pharaoh’s claim to be lord over his subjects means they must obey him and not devote themselves to another’s command.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r9.anchor: وأما ادعاؤه الربوبية لنفسه فبمعنى أنه يجب على من تحت يده طاعته والانقياد له وعدم الاشتغال بطاعة غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r10.claim: Even Pharaoh began an argument and requested proof rather than resorting to abuse; sophistry against a caller to truth is disgraceful, and Muslims should not approve what Pharaoh avoided.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r10.anchor: واستدل فى شروعه فى المناظرة وطلب الحجة دون السفاهة والشغب مع كونه جبارا شديد البطش

ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r11.claim: Moses’ proof exposes blind imitation and the error of claiming that knowledge of God comes from a messenger’s assertion; one may quote an opponent with the reply and must hear the objection to answer it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p202/r11.anchor: على فساد التقليد فى امثال هذا المطلوب وفساد قول القائل : أن معرفة الله تعالى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r6.speaker: الحسن، قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r6.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say God gave each thing what suits it and guided it to what makes it right.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r6.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة: أعطى كل شيء صلاحه، وهداه لما يصلحه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r7.claim: Mujahid says God gave every creature its form, distinct from other creatures, then guided it to its useful food, drink, and mate.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد: أعطى كل شيء صورته، لم يجعل خلق الإنسان كخلق البهائم، ولا خلق البهائم كخلق الإنسان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r8.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak says each body part was given its function: hands grasp, feet walk, tongues speak, eyes see, and ears hear.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r8.anchor: وقال الضحاك: "أعطى كل شيء خلقه: يعني اليد للبطش، والرجل للمشي، واللسان للنطق، والعين للنظر، والأذن للسمع.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r9.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says God gave each creature its mate and guided it to mating: woman, she-camel, female donkey, or mare.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r9.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: {أعطى كل شيء خلقه} يعني زوج، للإنسان المرأة، وللبعير الناقة، وللحمار الأتان، وللفرس الرمكة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r1.claim: God gave every kind its form and shape suited to the perfection possible for it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r1.anchor: صورته وشكله الذي يطابق كماله الممكن له

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r2.claim: Alternatively, God gave each creature what it needs and can use; the second object is advanced because that is the point being explained.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r2.anchor: كل شيء يحتاجون إليه ويرتفقون به، فقدم المفعول الثاني لأنه المقصود بيانه

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r3.claim: Another view is that every animal was given a mate matching it in creation and form.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r3.anchor: وقيل أعطى كل حيوان نظيره في الخلق والصورة زوجا

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r4.claim: A reading treats “khalqahu” as an adjective of its preceding noun or its possessor, unusually, with the second object understood as whatever benefits each creature.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r4.anchor: وقرىء { خلقه } صفة للمضاف إليه أو المضاف على شذوذ

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r5.claim: God then taught each creature, by instinct or choice, how to benefit from its gifts and attain survival and perfection.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r5.anchor: ثم عرفه كيف يرتفق بما أعطي وكيف يتوصل به إلى بقائه وكماله اختيارا أو طبعا

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r6.claim: Moses gives an exceptionally eloquent, concise answer encompassing all existence in its ranks and showing that God alone is self-sufficient, powerful, and the unrestricted benefactor, while all else depends on Him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r6.anchor: وهو جواب في غاية البلاغة لاختصاره وإعرابه عن الموجودات بأسرها على مراتبها

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r7.claim: The answer confounded the unbeliever and left him unable to counter it, so he could only change the subject.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:50/r7.anchor: ولذلك بهت الذي كفر وأفحم عن الدخل عليه فلم ير إلا صرف الكلام عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r9.claim: Moses answers immediately that their Lord is their creator, nurturer, and master.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r10.claim: God gives each existing thing its fitting form and qualities, including shape, size, color, temperament, benefits, and effects.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r10.anchor: أي ما هو عليه مما هو به أليق في المنافع المنوطة به

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r11.claim: God then guides every animal, rational or not, to its benefits and harms, so it pursues the former and avoids the latter.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r11.anchor: أي كل حيوان منه مع أن فيها العاقل وغيه إلى جميع منافعه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r12.claim: The word then marks the majesty of imparting spirit, beside which other differences diminish.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r12.anchor: في إفاضة الروح من الجلالة والعظم ما يضمحل عنده غيره من المفاوتة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r13.claim: The varied forms and guidance, despite creatures' equal relation to their maker, prove one freely choosing agent; nature governed by stars or other forces could not explain the differences.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r13.anchor: فثبت بهذه المفاوتة والمفاضلة مع اتحاد نسبة الكل إلى الفاعل أنه واحد مختار

DURR-FULL:v5p581/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r3.claim: God gave each creature its soul, then guided it to its mate, food, drink, and dwelling.
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه} قال: خلق لكل شيء روحه ثم {هدى} قال: هداه لمنكحه ومطعمه ومشربه ومسكنه

DURR-FULL:v5p581/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r4.claim: God gave each creature its counterpart, such as a man a woman, then guided it to sexual intercourse.
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {أعطى كل شيء خلقه} يقول: مثله أعطى الإنسان انسانة والحمار حمارة والشاة شاته

DURR-FULL:v5p581/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r5.claim: God gave each thing what would benefit it, then guided it to that benefit.
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r5.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله: {أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى} قال: أعطى كل شيء ما يصلحه ثم هداه له

DURR-FULL:v5p581/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r6.claim: God formed every animal and taught it what benefits it, making human and animal forms distinct; Mujahid links this to God's creation and measurement of all things.
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد - رضي الله عنه - في قوله: {أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى} قال: سوى خلق كل دابة ثم هداها لما يصلحها

DURR-FULL:v5p581/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r7.claim: God gave each kind what suits it, including its proper mate, without letting creatures control their own creation, provision, or mating; He guided each to its provision and partner.
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه في قوله: {أعطى كل شيء خلقه} قال: أعطى كل ذي خلق ما يصلحه

DURR-FULL:v5p581/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r8.claim: “He gave each thing its form” means each received its shape, and “then guided it” means guiding it to its livelihood.
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {أعطى كل شيء خلقه} قال: أعطى كل شيء صورته {ثم هدى} قال: لمعيشته

DURR-FULL:v5p581/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r9.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r9.claim: The camel illustrates guidance: it rises and waits for its owner to come.
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r9.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى} قال: ألم تر إلى البعير كيف يقوم لصاحبه ينتظره

DURR-FULL:v5p582/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r1.claim: He glosses “then guided” as knowing how the male approaches the female.
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ثم هدى} قال: كيف يأتي الذكر الأنثى

DURR-FULL:v5p582/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r2.speaker: ابن سابط
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r2.claim: Animals are guided in four ways: they know God as Lord, mate, find their livelihood, and fear death.
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r2.anchor: عن ابن سابط قال: ما أبهت البهائم فلم تبهم عن أربع: تعلم أن الله ربها ويأتي الذكر الأنثى وتهتدي لمعايشها وتخاف الموت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r4.claim: Moses establishes God's lordship over all things, reasoning from the universal to the particular: Pharaoh is among the things covered by كل شيء.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r4.anchor: وأجاب موسى بإثبات الربوبية لله لجميع الموجودات جريا على قاعدة الاستدلال بالكلية على الجزئية بحيث ينتظم من مجموعهما قياس ، فإن فرعون من جملة الأشياء ، فهو داخل في عموم { كل شيء }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r5.claim: Grammatically, كل شيء is the first object of أعطى and خلقه the second; خلق means bringing into existence, and the verb أعطى reminds hearers that creation is a blessing as well as proof of lordship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r5.anchor: و { كل شيء } مفعول أول ل { أعطى } . و { خلقه } مفعوله الثاني . والخلق : مصدر بمعنى الإيجاد . وجيء بفعل الإعطاء للتنبيه على أن الخلق والتكوين نعمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r6.claim: One possible reading takes خلق in the specific sense of giving form: God gave each being its distinctive shape, producing genera, species, classes, and individuals.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الخلق بالمعنى الأخص ، وهو الخلق على شكل مخصوص ، فهو بمعنى الجعل ، أي الذي أعطى كل شيء من الموجودات شكله المختص به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r7.claim: An alternative syntax makes كل شيء the second object and خلقه the first: God gave creatures what they need, as in 6:99; the construction permits both readings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { كل شيء } مفعولا ثانيا ل { أعطى } ومفعوله الأول { خلقه } ، أي أعطى خلقه ما يحتاجونه ، كقوله : { فأخرجنا به نبات كل شيء } ( الأنعام : 99 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r8.claim: The scope of كل is either conventional generality limited to things suited to receiving their forms, or distributive generality pairing each thing with its creation, like people mounting their own animals.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r8.anchor: والاستغراق المستفاد من ( كل ) عرفي ، أي كل شيء من شأنه أن يعطاه أصناف الخلق ويناسب المعطي ، أو هو استغراق على قصد التوزيع بمقابلة الأشياء بالخلق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r9.claim: Moses' argument asks whether Pharaoh gave each creature its form; Pharaoh knows he did not, so he should infer that God bestowed existence and blessings and believe in Him through this attribute.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r9.anchor: فإذا تأمل علم أن الرب هو الذي أفاض الوجود والنعم على الموجودات كلها ، فآمن به بعنوان هذه الصفة وتلك المعرفة الموصلة إلى الإعتقاد الحق .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r10.claim: Then marks both temporal and ranked sequence: after creating things, God guided them to their purposes and to truth after creation and blessing, as in 90:8–10 where He distinguishes the two paths with clear signs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r10.anchor: و ( ثم ) للترتيب بمعنييه الزمني والرتبي ، أي خلق الأشياء ثم هدى إلى ما خلقهم لأجله ، وهداهم إلى الحق بعد أن خلقهم ، وأفاض عليهم النعم

FARRA:v2p180/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p180/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p180/r2.claim: أعطى كل شيء خلقه may mean that God gave every creature its mate or kind: a human male a woman, a sheep a sheep, and a bull a cow.
FARRA:v2p180/r2.anchor: يقال: أعطى الذكر من الناس امرأة مثله من صنفه

FARRA:v2p180/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p180/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p180/r3.claim: ثم هدى means that He inspired the male toward the female to be approached.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p279#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p279#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p279#4/r1.claim: God gave each kind of creature its matching form, including a male its corresponding female.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p279#4/r1.anchor: أي أعطى كل ذكر خلقا مثله من الإناث

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p279#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p279#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p279#4/r2.claim: God then guided the male to approach the female.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r1.claim: Moses takes the answer himself because Pharaoh addressed him specifically, then states divine attributes that leave Pharaoh no share in them, even figuratively.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r1.anchor: استبد موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم من حيث خصه في السؤال ثم أعلمه من صفات الله تعالى بأن لا شرك لفرعون فيه ولا بوجه مجاز

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r2.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r2.claim: One group says God gave male animals their kind and form as females, then guided them to mate.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r2.anchor: فقالت فرقة معناه أعطى الذكران من كل الحيوان نوعه وخلقته أنثى ثم هدى للإتيان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r3.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r3.claim: Another group says God gave every creature its form perfected and guided it to its benefits; the author prefers this as nobler and more comprehensive.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r3.anchor: قالت فرقة بل المعنى أعطى كل موجود من مخلوقاته خلقته وصورته، أي أكمل ذلك له وأتقنه ثم هدى أي يسر كل شيء لمنافعه ومرافقه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r4.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r4.claim: A reading with fatḥ on the lām in khalqahu leaves the second object of gave implicit, such as its completeness or form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47/r4.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «خلقه» بفتح اللام ويكون المفعول الثاني ب أعطى مقدرا تقديره كماله أو خلقته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r1.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r1.claim: One view says God gave each thing its form, creating distinct forms for each species; al-Dahhak reports it from Ibn ʿAbbas, and Mujahid and Saʿid ibn Jubayr agree.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r1.anchor: روى هذا المعنى الضحاك عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r2.claim: Another view says God gave each male its mate, so every animal received a compatible partner; it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas and held by al-Suddi.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r2.anchor: والثاني أعطى كل ذكر زوجه رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس وبه قال السدي فيكون المعنى أعطى كل حيوان ما يشاكله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r3.claim: Qatada says God gave each thing what is suitable for it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r3.anchor: والثالث أعطى كل شيء ما يصلحه قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس وابن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r4.claim: One interpretation of ‘then guided’ is that God showed each creature how the male approaches the female.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r4.anchor: أحدها هدى كيف يأتي الذكر الأنثى رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس وبه قال ابن جبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r5.claim: Another says God guided creatures to their mating place, food, and dwelling.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r5.anchor: والثاني هدى للمنكح والمطعم والمسكن رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r6.claim: Mujahid says God guided everything to its livelihood.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r6.anchor: والثالث هدى كل شيء إلى معيشته قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r7.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وابن عباس والأعمش وابن السميفع ونصير عن الكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r7.claim: ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Aʿmash, Ibn al-Sumayfaʿ, and Nasir from al-Kisaʾi read khalqahu with a fatḥa on lām.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن الخطاب وابن عباس والأعمش وابن السميفع ونصير عن الكسائي أعطى كل شيء خلقه بفتح اللام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r8.claim: The argument against Pharaoh is that the existence of creation and guidance proves there must be a Creator and a Guide.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291#2/r8.anchor: أنه قد ثبت وجود خلق وهداية فلا بد من خالق وهاد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the verse as God creating a mate for every thing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r2.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس يقول: خلق لكل شيء زوجة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r3.claim: As transmitted by al-Dahhak, Ibn ʿAbbās says God made a human human, a donkey a donkey, and a sheep a sheep.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك عن ابن عباس: جعل الإنسان إنسانا، والحمار حمارا، والشاة شاة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r4.claim: Mujahid, through al-Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, says God gave each thing its form.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r4.anchor: وقال ليث بن أبي سليم، عن مجاهد: أعطى كل شيء صورته.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r5.claim: Mujahid, through Ibn Abi Najih, says God fashioned the creation of every creature.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: سوى خلق كل دابة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r6.claim: Saʿid says God fitted every kind to its own form and needs, gave it fitting mating, and made none share His acts of creation, provision, and mating.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r6.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير في قوله: {أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى} قال: أعطى كل ذي خلق ما يصلحه من خلقه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r7.claim: Some exegetes equate the phrase with 87:3: God decreed destinies, deeds, lifespans, and provisions, then guided creatures along them so none can depart.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين: {أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى} كقوله تعالى: {والذي قدر فهدى} [الأعلى: 3] أي: قدر قدرا

JISHUMI:v7p4672/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r6.speaker: نصير عن الكسائي
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r6.claim: Nusayr transmits al-Kisai's reading of khalqahu with a fatḥa on the lām as a past-tense verb; a similar reading is attributed to Ibn Abbas.
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r6.anchor: روى نصير عن الكسائي: كل شيء خلقه بفتح اللام على فعل ماض، وروي نحوه عن ابن عباس،

JISHUMI:v7p4672/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r7.speaker: القراء
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r7.claim: The readers otherwise give the lām sukūn, treating khalq as a noun.
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r7.anchor: والقراء على سكون اللام على أنه اسم.

JISHUMI:v7p4676/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r2.claim: Only those who follow guidance are saved, so innovators have no salvation.
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن النجاة لمن اتبع الهدى، فتدل على أنه لا نجاة للمبتدعة.

JISHUMI:v7p4676/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r3.claim: God is known through His acts; this refutes reliance on imitation, necessity, inspiration, and the anthropomorphists' position.
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r3.anchor: ويدل قوله: (ربنا الذي أعطى) أنه تعالى يعرف بأفعاله لا طريق سوى ذلك، فيبطل قول من يقول بالتقليد، والضرورة، والإلهام، وقول المشبهة.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r3.claim: “His creation” may be the first object of “gave”: God gave each creature everything it needs and can use.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r3.anchor: أول مفعولي أعطى ، أي : أعطى خليقته كل شيء يحتاجون إليه ويرتفقون به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r4.claim: Alternatively, it is the second object: God gave every thing a form suited to its function, as the eye, ear, nose, limbs, and tongue suit their uses.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r4.anchor: أو ثانيهما ، أي : أعطى كل شيء صورته وشكله الذي يطابق المنفعة المنوطة به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r5.claim: Alternatively, God gave each animal a matching counterpart of its own kind, including male and female pairs among livestock and people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r5.anchor: والبعير والناقة ، والرجل والمرأة ، فلم يزاوج منها شيئا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r6.claim: A reading treats “His creation” as an adjective of either adjoining noun, meaning that God did not withhold His gift and favor from anything He created.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r6.anchor: أي : كل شيء خلقه الله لم يخله من عطائه وإنعامه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r7.claim: “Then He guided” means that God taught each creature how to benefit from what it was given and how to obtain it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r7.anchor: أي عرف كيف يرتفق بما أعطى ، وكيف يتوصل إليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r8.claim: The author praises Moses' answer as concise, comprehensive, and clear to a fair-minded person seeking truth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r8.anchor: ولله در هذا الجواب ما أخصره وما أجمعه ، وما أبينه لمن ألقى الذهن ونظر بعين الإنصاف

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r1.claim: God gave each creature its mate of the same kind and guided it to mate with it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r1.anchor: أحدها : أعطى كل شيء زوجه من جنسه , ثم هداه لنكاحه ، قاله ابن عباس والسدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r2.claim: God gave each creature its form and guided it to its livelihood, food, and drink; a poem uses khalq to mean form.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r2.anchor: الثاني : أعطى كل شيء صورته , ثم هداه إلى معيشته ومطعمه ومشربه , قاله مجاهد قال الشاعر :

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r3.claim: A poetic line illustrates khalqa as the form or image of a thing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r3.anchor: قال الشاعر : وله في كل شيء خلقه وكذلك الله ما شاء فعل … يعني بالخلقة الصورة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r4.claim: God gave every thing what would set it right, then guided it to that.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r4.anchor: الثالث : أعطى كلا ما يصلحه , ثم هداه له , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r5.claim: A fourth possibility is that God gave each creature its inspired knowledge or craft and guided it to recognize it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405#2/r5.anchor: ويحتمل رابعا : أعطى كل شيء ما ألهمه من علم أو صناعة وهداه إلى معرفته .

MUJAHID:v1p397#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p397#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p397#3/r1.claim: God gave each creature its proper form.
MUJAHID:v1p397#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ أعطى كل شيء خلقه ﴾ قال سوى خلق كل دابة

MUJAHID:v1p397#3/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p397#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p397#3/r2.claim: God then guided each creature to what would benefit it and taught it that guidance.
MUJAHID:v1p397#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ ثم هدى ﴾ يقول هداها لما يصلحها فعلمها إياه

MUQATIL:20:48-53/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:48-53/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:48-53/r3.claim: God gave every animal its fitting form, then guided it to its livelihood and pasture; some eat grain and others meat.
MUQATIL:20:48-53/r3.anchor: { قال ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء } من الدواب { خلقه } يعنى صورته التى تصلح له

NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#2/r1.claim: If khalqahu is the first object of aʿṭā, God gave each thing its constitution and everything needed for its use; if it is the second object, He gave each thing a form suited to its function, such as the eye for sight and ear for hearing.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#2/r1.anchor: أول مفعولي أعطي أي أعطى حليقته كل شيء يحتاجون إليه ويرتفقون به أو ثانيهما أي أعطي كل شيء صورته وشكله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#2/r2.speaker: نصير
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#2/r2.claim: Naṣīr reads khalqahu adjectivally with either the annexed noun or its complement, meaning God gave every created thing a provision.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ نصير خلقه صفة للمضاف أو للمضاف إليه أي أعطي كل شيء مخلوق عطاء

NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#2/r3.claim: Then God guided each creature, directing it to what it needs.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#2/r4.claim: God’s guidance directs creatures toward livelihood in this world and happiness in the next.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#2/r4.anchor: بما أعطى للمعيشة في الدنيا والسعادة في العقبى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r15.claim: God is known by His attributes as creator of the world, not by a personal proper name; the singular response indicates Moses alone spoke.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r15.anchor: أي أنه يعرف بصفاته، وليس له اسم علم حتى يقال فلان، بل هو خالق العالم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r16.claim: One grammatical parse makes “his creation” the first object of “gave”; another makes it the second, meaning each creature received its useful form, as al-Dahhak explains below.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r16.anchor: «وخلقه» أول مفعولي أعطى، أي أعطى خليقته كل شيء يحتاجون إليه ويرتفقون به، أو ثانيهما

QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r17.speaker: ابن عباس، سعيد بن جبير، السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r17.claim: God gave each thing a mate of its kind and guided it to mating, food, drink, and dwelling.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r17.anchor: قال ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير والسدي: أعطى كل شيء زوجه من جنسه، ثم هداه إلى منكحه ومطعمه ومشربه ومسكنه.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r18.claim: An additional explanation is that God guided creatures toward affection, companionship, and marriage.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r18.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: ثم هداه إلى الألفة والاجتماع والمناكحة.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r19.speaker: الحسن، قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r19.claim: God gave each thing what is right for it and guided it to what improves it.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r19.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة: أعطى كل شيء صلاحه، وهداه لما يصلحه.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r1.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r1.claim: God gave each creature its own form, distinguishing human creation from animal creation, and formed and measured everything.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r1.anchor: وقال مجاهد: أعطى كل شيء صورة لم يجعل خلق الإنسان في خلق البهائم، ولا خلق البهائم في خلق الإنسان

QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r2.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r2.claim: The cited verse of poetry uses khalqa to mean a creature's form or image.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r2.anchor: وله في كل شيء خلقة وكذاك الله ما شاء فعل يعني بالخلقة الصورة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r3.speaker: عطية، مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r3.claim: They also take khalqa to mean form or image.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r4.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r4.claim: God gave each creature the benefit suited to it: hands grasp, feet walk, tongues speak, eyes see, and ears hear.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك: أعطى كل شيء خلقه من المنفعة المنوطة به المطابقة له. يعني اليد للبطش، والرجل للمشي

QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r5.claim: Another view is that God gave each creature the knowledge or craft He inspired it with.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r5.anchor: وقيل: أعطى كل شيء ما ألهمه من علم أو صناعة.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r6.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r6.claim: God formed males for females and guided each male to the female suited to him; “each thing” means each like its kind.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r6.anchor: وقال الفراء: خلق الرجل للمرأة، ولكل ذكر ما يوافقه من الإناث، ثم هدى الذكر للأنثى.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r7.claim: Al-Qurtubi identifies al-Farra's explanation with Ibn Abbas's view.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r7.anchor: فالتقدير على هذا أعطى كل شيء مثل خلقه. قلت: وهذا معنى قول ابن عباس.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r8.claim: The verse's general wording encompasses all the reported interpretations.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r9.speaker: الأعمش
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r9.claim: Al-Aʿmash is reported by Zāʾida to read khalaqahu with fatḥa on the lām; this reading is also attributed to Ibn Abi Ishaq and narrated by Nasir from al-Kisaʾi and others.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r9.anchor: وروى زائدة عن الأعمش أنه قرأ «الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه» بفتح اللام وهي قراءة ابن أبي إسحاق ورواها نصير عن الكسائي وغيره

QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r10.claim: On this reading, God gave human beings everything He created that they need; both readings agree in meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:50/r10.anchor: أي أعطى بني آدم كل شيء خلقه مما يحتاجون إليه. فالقراءتان متفقتان في المعنى.

RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r4.claim: They infer Pharaoh knew the proposition in Moses’ description of the Lord, because the relative clause presents a complete known description.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r4.anchor: قول موسى عليه السلام ههنا : { ربنا الذى أعطى كل شىء خلقه ثم هدى } وكلمة الذي تقتضي وصف المعرفة بجملة معلومة

RAZI-FULL:v22p56#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p56#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p56#2/r1.claim: Moses proves the Creator from creatures; Razi links this argument to the command to praise God as creator and guide and to Abraham’s declaration that the Lord of the worlds created and guides him.
RAZI-FULL:v22p56#2/r1.anchor: هذه الدلالة هي التي ذكرها الله تعالى لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله : { سبح اسم ربك الاعلى * الذى خلق فسوى * والذى قدر فهدى }

RAZI-FULL:v22p56#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p56#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p56#2/r2.claim: Razi proposes that creation means forming bodies and guidance means originating their cognitive and motive faculties, so bodily formation comes first.
RAZI-FULL:v22p56#2/r2.anchor: يشبه أن يكون الخلق عبارة عن تركيب القوالب والأبدان والهداية عبارة عن إبداع القوى المدركة والمحركة في تلك الأجسام

RAZI-FULL:v22p56#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p56#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p56#2/r3.claim: Razi supports the order of formation before guidance with the creation of Adam’s form before the spirit and the successive stages of human creation.
RAZI-FULL:v22p56#2/r3.anchor: وعلى هذا التقدير يكون الخلق مقدما على الهداية ولذلك قال : { فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحى } ( الحجر : 29 )

RAZI-FULL:v22p56#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p56#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p56#2/r4.claim: The human body reverses the expected elemental order: earth-like bone and hair are highest, while fire-like heat in the heart is lowest, demonstrating wise divine design rather than natural necessity.
RAZI-FULL:v22p56#2/r4.anchor: ثم إنه سبحانه قلب هذا الترتيب في خلقة الإنسان فجعل أعلى الأشياء منه العظم والشعر وهما أيبس ما في البدن

RAZI-FULL:v22p56#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p56#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p56#2/r5.claim: The hexagonal construction of bees’ cells and insects’ guidance to their own interests require inspiration by an omniscient manager.
RAZI-FULL:v22p56#2/r5.anchor: عجائب النحل في تركيب البيوت المسدسة وعجائب أحوال البق والبعوض في اهتدائها إلى مصالح أنفسها

RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r1.claim: God supplies creatures with food, drink, clothing, and mates, then guides them in using these gifts, including refining materials, preparing medicines, and combining ingredients to improve food.
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r1.anchor: أنه تعالى هو الذي أنعم على الخلائق بما به قوامهم من المطعوم والمشروب والملبوس والمنكوح ثم هداهم إلى كيفية الانتفاع بها

RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r2.claim: This guidance extends beyond humans: creatures are directed to mates and offspring to their mothers’ breasts.
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r2.anchor: وهذا غير مختص بالإنسان بل عام في جميع الحيوانات فأعطى الإنسان إنسانة والحمار حمارة والبعير ناقة ثم هداه لها

RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r3.claim: Guidance also appears in each organ’s design and power, such as hands grasping and feet walking, and in the coordination of organs into one person.
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r3.anchor: بل هذا غير مختص بالحيوانات بل هو حاصل في أعضائها فإنه خلق اليد على تركيب خاص وأودع فيها قوة الأخذ وخلق الرجل على تركيب خاص

RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r4.claim: The arrangement, powers, and guidance of bodies cannot be necessary features, since death shows bodies separated from those arrangements and capacities; they are contingent and need a cause.
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r4.anchor: إما أن يكون واجبا أو جائزا والأول باطل لأنا نشاهد تلك الأجسام بعد الموت منفكة عن تلك التراكيب والقوى فدل على أن ذلك جائز

RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r5.claim: Neither a person nor their parents can be the cause of this design: people cannot change even a hair and know little of the benefits of their organs despite anatomical study.
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r5.anchor: وليس ذلك المرجح هو الإنسان ولا أبواه لأن فعل ذلك يستدعي قدرة عليه وعلما بما فيه من المصالح والمفاسد

RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r6.claim: The designer cannot be a body, since a body’s own causal specification would itself be contingent and require another cause, leading to an impossible regress.
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r6.anchor: وذلك الموجود لا يجوز أن يكون جسما لأن الأجسام متساوية في الجسمية فاختصاص ذلك الجسم بتلك المؤثرية لا بد وأن يكون جائزا

RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r7.claim: The causal chain must end in an incorporeal, necessary existent who manages creation.
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r7.anchor: فلا بد من الانتهاء في سلسلة الحاجة / إلى موجود مؤثر ومدبر ليس بجسم ولا جسماني

RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r8.claim: The manager acts by choice rather than by nature: a necessary cause acting by nature would not differentiate among equal bodies, though they receive celestial, elemental, vegetal, and animal forms.
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r8.anchor: ثم تأثير ذلك المؤثر إما أن يكون بالذات أو بالاختيار ، والأول محال لأن الموجب لا يميز مثلا عن مثل

RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r9.claim: Such marvelous voluntary action requires knowledge, and the manager must be necessary in essence and attributes to avoid another infinite causal regress.
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r9.anchor: فثبت أن المؤثر والمدبر قادر والقادر لا يمكنه مثل هذه الأفعال العجيبة إلا إذا كان عالما

RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r10.claim: Because the necessary being’s power and knowledge cannot be limited to selected possibilities, this proof establishes God as omniscient and omnipotent.
RAZI-FULL:v22p57/r10.anchor: وإذا كان واجب الوجود في قادريته وعالميته والواجب لذاته لا يتخصص ببعض الممكنات دون البعض وجب ( أن ) يكون عالما بكل ما صح أن يكون معلوما

RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r1.claim: Razi offers two reasons Pharaoh addressed both Moses and Aaron but then singled out Moses: Moses was the principal prophet and Aaron his minister, or Pharaoh exploited Moses’ stutter and Aaron’s greater eloquence.
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r1.anchor: أن فرعون خاطب الاثنين بقوله : { فمن ربكما } ثم وجه النداء إلى أحدهما وهو موسى عليه السلام لأنه الأصل في النبوة وهرون وزيره وتابعه

RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r3.claim: Razi gives two readings of the phrase: either God gave each creature everything it needs, with the wording advanced, or God gave each thing a form matching its benefit and purpose.
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r3.anchor: في قوله : { الذى أعطى كل شىء خلقه ثم هدى } وجهان : أحدهما : التقديم والتأخير أي أعطى خلقه كل شيء يحتاجون إليه

RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r4.claim: On the second reading, creation means a form and shape matched to each thing’s benefit and welfare.
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r4.anchor: أن يكون المراد من الخلق الشكل والصورة المطابقة للمنفعة فكأنه سبحانه قال : أعطى كل شيء الشكل الذي يطابق منفعته ومصلحته

RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r5.claim: A reading treats “its creation” as an adjective of either the annexed noun or its complement, meaning God has bestowed favor on everything He created.
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r5.anchor: وقرىء خلقه صفة للمضاف أو المضاف إليه ، والمعنى أن كل شيء خلقه الله لم يخله من إعطائه وإنعامه

RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r2.claim: After the general proof covering people, animals, plants, and inanimate things, Moses offers specific proofs; the first is that God made the earth a cradle.
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r2.anchor: لما ذكر الدلالة الأولى وهي دلالة عامة تتناول جميع المخلوقات من الإنسان وسائر الحيوانات وأنواع النبات والجمادات ذكر بعد ذلك دلائل خاصة وهي ثلاثة

STUDYQURAN:20:49/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:49/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:49/r4.claim: Moses answers by pointing to signs of God's Being, as giver of each thing's creation and guidance; Pharaoh then asks about divine essence.
STUDYQURAN:20:49/r4.anchor: When Moses answered Pharaoh by pointing to the signs of God’s Being, citing Him as He Who gives everything its creation, then guides [it]

STUDYQURAN:20:49/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:49/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:49/r5.claim: God's essence is beyond all description or definition and inaccessible through human means.
STUDYQURAN:20:49/r5.anchor: God’s Essence is above any and all descriptions and definitions and is completely inaccessible through human means

SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r1.claim: With كل شيء as first object and خلقه as second, the phrase can mean each thing received a form suited to its function, such as eye to sight and ear to hearing.
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r1.anchor: في هذه الآية وجهان: أحدهما: أن يكون " كل شيء " مفعولا أول، و " خلقه " مفعولا ثانيا على معنى: أعطى كل شيء شكله وصورته، الذي يطابق المنفعة المنوطة به

SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r2.claim: The same syntax can mean God paired each animal with its matching kind, without pairing it with an unlike species.
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r2.anchor: كما أعطى العين الهيئة التي تطابق الإبصار، والأذن الشكل الذي يطابق الاستماع ويوافقه

SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r3.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r3.claim: Another gloss is that God gave each created thing its creation, meaning He originated it.
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r3.anchor: وقيل: المعنى: أعطى كل شيء مخلوق خلقه أي: هو الذي ابتدعه.

SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r4.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r4.claim: Another gloss is that every created thing received its fitting, perfected shape and measure.
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r4.anchor: وقيل: المعنى: أعطى كل شيء مما خلق خلقته وصورته على ما يناسبه من الإتقان.

SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r5.claim: Alternatively, خلقه is the first object and كل شيء the second, fronted; God gave creatures everything they need and use.
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r5.anchor: والثاني: أن يكون " كل شيء " مفعولا ثانيا، و " خلقه " هو الأول، فقدم الثاني عليه

SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r6.speaker: عبد الله والحسن والأعمش وأبو نهيك وابن أبي إسحاق ونصير عن الكسائي وناس من أصحاب رسول الله
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r6.claim: These readers pronounce the lām of خلقه with fatḥa, making it a past-tense verb.
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r6.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله والحسن والأعمش وأبو نهيك وابن أبي إسحاق ونصير عن الكسائي وناس من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم " خلقه " بفتح اللام فعلا ماضيا.

SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r7.claim: On the verbal reading, the clause can modify كل or شيء; its second object may be elided as recoverable, meaning what each thing needs or its completion.
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r7.anchor: وهذه الجملة في هذه القراءة تحتمل أن تكون منصوبة المحل صفة ل " كل " أو في محل جر صفة ل " شيء "

SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r8.claim: The second object may instead be omitted absolutely: every thing God created received His bounty and gift.
SAMIN-DURR:20:50/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون حذفه حذف اقتصار، والمعنى: أن كل شيء خلقه الله لم يخله من إنعامه وعطائه.

TAB-FULL:v16p79/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p79/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p79/r2.claim: God gave each kind a matching mate in form, and did not pair humans with animals; He then guided creatures to reproduction and their other needs for food and drink.
TAB-FULL:v16p79/r2.anchor: كالذكور من بني آدم، أعطاهم نظير خلقهم من الإناث أزواجا، وكالذكور من البهائم

TAB-FULL:v16p79/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p79/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p79/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says God created a mate for everything and guided it to mating, food, drink, dwelling, and birth.
TAB-FULL:v16p79/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى} [طه: 50] يقول: خلق لكل شيء زوجة

TAB-FULL:v16p79/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p79/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v16p79/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says every animal received a mate and was guided to mating.
TAB-FULL:v16p79/r4.anchor: عن السدي: {قال ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى} [طه: 50] يقول: أعطى كل دابة خلقها زوجا

TAB-FULL:v16p79/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p79/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p79/r5.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says God guided creatures to one another, joined their hearts, and guided them to marry one another.
TAB-FULL:v16p79/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى} [طه: 50] يعني: هدى بعضهم إلى بعض

TAB-FULL:v16p79/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p79/r6.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v16p79/r6.claim: Others interpret the gift as each creature's own shape and say God guided it to what sustains it, including means of obtaining food and livelihood.
TAB-FULL:v16p79/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى ذلك: أعطى كل شيء صورته، وهي خلقه الذي خلقه به

TAB-FULL:v16p81/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r1.claim: Mujahid says God gave everything its form and guided it to its livelihood.
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى} [طه: 50] قال: أعطى كل شيء صورته ثم هدى كل شيء إلى معيشته

TAB-FULL:v16p81/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r2.claim: Mujahid also says God fashioned each creature and taught it what benefits it.
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى} [طه: 50] قال: سوى خلق كل دابة، ثم هداها لما يصلحها، فعلمها إياه

TAB-FULL:v16p81/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r3.claim: Mujahid says God made every creature fit its own kind, not human-shaped animals or animal-shaped humans, and measured everything precisely.
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد، قوله: {ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى} [طه: 50] قال: سوى خلق كل دابة

TAB-FULL:v16p81/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r4.claim: A further report from Mujahid says God guided each creature to its skill and livelihood.
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r4.anchor: عن حميد عن مجاهد {أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى} [طه: 50] قال: هداه إلى حيلته ومعيشته

TAB-FULL:v16p81/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r5.claim: Qatāda interprets the gift as whatever is beneficial to each thing, with God then guiding it to that benefit.
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {أعطى كل شيء خلقه} [طه: 50] قال: أعطى كل شيء ما يصلحه. ثم هداه له

TAB-FULL:v16p81/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r6.claim: Al-Tabari rejects taking the phrase to mean that God gave each creature itself: a gift requires a giver, recipient, and gift, while a creature's form is only one of its parts.
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r6.anchor: ولا يعطي المعطي نفسه، بل إنما يعطي ما هو غيره، لأن العطية تقتضي المعطي والمعطى والعطية

TAB-FULL:v16p81/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r7.claim: He therefore prefers that God gave each thing a counterpart like its own created kind, then guided it as described earlier.
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r7.anchor: فالأصوب من معانيه أن يكون موجها إلى أن كل شيء أعطاه ربه مثل خلقه، فزوجه به، ثم هداه

TAB-FULL:v16p81/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r8.claim: The wording suppresses the word “like,” as Arabic may call a person a lion after first saying he is like a lion.
TAB-FULL:v16p81/r8.anchor: كما يقال: عبد الله مثل الأسد، ثم يحذف مثل، فيقول: عبد الله الأسد

TABATABAI:20:49-79/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r1.claim: Guidance means showing a thing the path to its goal or conveying it there; both reduce to connecting it with what it seeks.
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r1.anchor: والهداية إراءة الشيء الطريق الموصل إلى مطلوبة أو إيصاله إلى مطلوبه ويعود المعنيان في الحقيقة إلى معنى واحد

TABATABAI:20:49-79/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r2.claim: Because guidance is unqualified and the only antecedent is each thing given its creation, it means guiding every thing toward the end for which it exists.
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r2.anchor: فالظاهر أن المراد هداية كل شيء

TABATABAI:20:49-79/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r3.claim: God links each thing's innate powers and instruments to the effects that carry it toward its final end; a human embryo is equipped to become a complete human.
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r3.anchor: إلقائه الرابطة بين كل شيء بما جهز به في وجوده من القوى والالات وبين آثاره التي تنتهي به إلى غايه وجوده

TABATABAI:20:49-79/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r4.claim: The conjunction 'then' marks rank order: a thing's movement toward its end follows its existence; for bodily beings this unfolding is gradual in time.
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r4.anchor: وأن المراد التأخر الرتبي فإن سير الشيء وحركته بعد وجوده رتبة

TABATABAI:20:49-79/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r5.claim: This is universal guidance, not guidance unique to humans: everything is equipped to move toward its own perfection, and God is the guide.
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r5.anchor: فكل شيء مهدي نحو كماله بما جهز به من تجهيز والله سبحانه هو الهادي

TABATABAI:20:49-79/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r6.claim: The systems of interaction among things, both particular and universal, instantiate divine guidance and, from another perspective, divine governance.
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r6.anchor: نظام الفعل والانفعال في الأشياء وإن شئت فقل النظام الجزئي الخاص بكل شيء والنظام العام الجامع لجميع الأنظمة الجزئية

TABATABAI:20:49-79/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r7.claim: Governance ultimately depends on creation: the one who brings things into being is also the one to whom their existence and attributes belong.
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r7.anchor: أن الذي ينتهي وينتسب إليه تدبير الأشياء هو الذي أوجد نفس الأشياء فكل وجود أو صفة وجود ينتهي إليه

TABATABAI:20:49-79/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r8.claim: The verse proves God alone is Lord: creating things entails owning their existence, since they depend on him, and owning their governance.
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r8.anchor: مشتمل على البرهان على كونه تعالى رب كل شيء لا رب غيره فإن خلقه الأشياء وإيجاده لها يستلزم ملكه لوجوداتها

TABATABAI:20:49-79/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r9.claim: In response to Pharaoh's evasive question, 'Lord of all worlds' would assert the claim, but 'the one who gave everything its creation and guided it' also supplies its proof.
TABATABAI:20:49-79/r9.anchor: فأجيب بما هو أبلغ من ذلك فقيل

TABATABAI:20:49-79#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#2/r1.claim: The verse emphasizes guidance rather than governance because the context is a call to guidance, to which universal guidance is especially suited.

TABATABAI:20:49-79#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:20:49-79#2/r2.claim: One interpretation takes 'its creation' to mean its counterpart, so God gave each thing a mate, as in the verse about creating pairs.

TABATABAI:20:49-79#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:20:49-79#2/r3.claim: Another interpretation treats 'everything' as kinds of blessings and 'creation' as created beings: God gave his creatures every blessing.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#2/r3.anchor: وقول بعضهم إن المراد بكل شيء أنواع النعم وهو مفعول ثان لأعطى وبالخلق المخلوق

TABATABAI:20:49-79#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:20:49-79#2/r4.claim: A further interpretation says God gave each thing its sought existence according to its disposition, then guided people to his existence and unity.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#2/r4.anchor: وقول بعضهم إن المراد بالهداية الإرشاد والدلالة على وجوده تعالى ووحدته بلا شريك

TABATABAI:20:49-79#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#2/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects these alternatives as remote from the context and as restricting the verse's wording without evidence.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#2/r5.anchor: فإنما هي معان بعيدة عن السياق وتقييدات للفظ الآية من غير مقيد

ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r1.claim: God created each thing in the form most useful and suitable to it, then guided it to its livelihood.
ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r1.anchor: معناه خلق كل شيء على الهيئة التي بها ينتفع، والتي هي أصلح الخلق له،

ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r2.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r2.claim: Another possible gloss says God guided each creature to the place where its offspring is produced; males instinctively approach females without prior instruction.
