ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r2.anchor: وقد قيل ثم هداه لموضع ما يكون منه الولد.

ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r3.claim: The first, broader interpretation is clearer and includes reproductive guidance as part of what benefits each creature.
ZAJJAJ:v3p358#2/r3.anchor: والقول الأول ينتظم هذا المعنى، لأنه إذا هداه لمصلحته

TABRISI:20:52-53/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53/r1.speaker: نصر عن الكسائي
TABRISI:20:52-53/r1.claim: Naṣr transmits from al-Kisāʾī a reading with an open lām in khalqahu; the other readers pronounce the lām quiescent.
TABRISI:20:52-53/r1.anchor: قرأ نصر عن الكسائي خلقه بفتح اللام

TABRISI:20:52-53/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:52-53/r2.claim: With the quiescent lām, the phrase means God gave each thing its form, creating every animal in its own shape and then guiding it.
TABRISI:20:52-53/r2.anchor: أعطى كل شيء صورته أي خلق كل حيوان

TABRISI:20:52-53/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:52-53/r3.claim: With the open lām, the clause describes the thing in the genitive and leaves the second object of gave implicit: God gives each created thing what His ordering requires, then guides it.
TABRISI:20:52-53/r3.anchor: بفتح اللام فإنه جملة من الفعل والفاعل في موضع جر

TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد وعطية ومقاتل
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r8.claim: Mujāhid, ʿAṭiyyah, and Muqātil say God gave each thing its proper form and then guided it to food, drink, mating, and other needs.

TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Suddī interpret this as giving each creature its mate of its own kind and guiding it to mate.

TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r10.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r10.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says God gave His creatures worldly blessings to eat, drink, and use, and guided them to livelihoods and religious matters leading to afterlife blessings.

THALABI:v6p246/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p246/r12.speaker: الحسين وقتادة
THALABI:v6p246/r12.claim: Al-Husayn and Qatada say God gave each thing what makes it sound and guided it to what benefits it.
THALABI:v6p246/r12.anchor: قال الحسين وقتادة: أعطى كل شيء صلاحه وهداه لما يصلحه.

THALABI:v6p247/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p247/r1.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p247/r1.claim: Mujahid says God did not create humans in the form of beasts or beasts in the form of humans; He created each thing and measured it precisely.
THALABI:v6p247/r1.anchor: وقال مجاهد: لم يجعل الإنسان في خلق البهائم، ولا خلق البهائم في خلق الإنسان، ولكن خلق كل شي فقدره تقديرا.

THALABI:v6p247/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p247/r2.speaker: عطية
THALABI:v6p247/r2.claim: ʿAtiyya interprets giving each thing its creation as giving it its form.
THALABI:v6p247/r2.anchor: وقال عطية: أعطى كل شيء خلقه يعني صورته.

THALABI:v6p247/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p247/r3.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v6p247/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak explains that God gave each creature its fitting faculties: hands to grasp, legs to walk, tongues to speak, eyes to see, and ears to hear.
THALABI:v6p247/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك: أعطى كل شيء خلقه، يعني اليد للبطش والرجل للمشي واللسان للنطق والعين للبصر والأذن للسمع.

THALABI:v6p247/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p247/r4.speaker: إسماعيل بن أبي صالح
THALABI:v6p247/r4.claim: Ismaʿil ibn Abi Salih says God guided every creature to its livelihood.
THALABI:v6p247/r4.anchor: عن إسماعيل بن أبي صالح، أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى قال: هداه لمعيشته.

THALABI:v6p247/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p247/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v6p247/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and Saʿid ibn Jubayr take the phrase to mean each creature received its form or mate: humans a wife, camels a she-camel, horses a mare, and donkeys a female; God then taught them mating.
THALABI:v6p247/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير: أعطى كل شيء خلقه يعني شكله، للإنسان الزوجة وللبعير الناقة وللفرس الرمكة وللحمار الأتان

THALABI:v6p247/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p247/r6.speaker: نصير
THALABI:v6p247/r6.claim: Nusayr reads khalqahu with fatḥa on the lām, making it a verb.
THALABI:v6p247/r6.anchor: وقرأ نصير خلقه بفتح اللام على الفعل.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p413#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p413#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p413#2/r4.claim: The singular قال ربنا supports that Moses alone answered; if both brothers were addressed, they would have answered together.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p413#2/r4.anchor: ويدل على أن المخاطب موسى دون هارون قوله تعالى: {قال ربنا} ولم يقل: قالا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r1.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r1.claim: God formed humans unlike beasts and beasts unlike humans, giving every creature its measured creation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r1.anchor: ما قاله مجاهد وهو أنه قال: (لم يجعل خلق الإنسان كخلق البهائم، ولا خلق البهائم كخلق الإنسان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r2.speaker: عطية، ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r2.claim: They take ‘gave each thing its creation’ to mean that God gave it its form, each animal kind having a distinct form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r2.anchor: قال عطية، ومقاتل: ({أعطى كل شيء خلقه} يعني صورته)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r3.speaker: الحسن، وقتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r3.claim: They interpret the phrase as giving each thing its fitness and what makes it sound; its form suits its purpose.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن، وقتادة: (أعطى كل شيء صلاحه وما يصلحه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r4.claim: On this interpretation, God gave each thing the form that suits what it was created to do, then guided it to its livelihood, food, mate, and other needs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r4.anchor: هداه لما يصلحه من معيشته ومشربه ومنكحه إلى غير ذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq prefers that God created each thing in the form most useful and fitting for it, then guided it to its livelihood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r5.anchor: اختيار أبي إسحاق وبينه فقال: (معناه: خلق كل شيء على الهيئة التي بها ينتفع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r6.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r6.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as God perfecting everything He created.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r6.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: (يريد أتقن كل ما خلق)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r7.speaker: الكلبي، والسدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r7.claim: Their second interpretation is that God paired each creature with a mate of its own kind, such as man with woman and camel with she-camel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r7.anchor: قول الكلبي، والسدي قالا: (أعطى الرجل المرأة، والبعير الناقة، والذكر الأنثى من جنسه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r8.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says God guided the male to intercourse with the female of its kind.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r8.anchor: صرح السدي بهذا اللفظ قال: (أعطى الذكر الأنثى مثل خلقه (ثم هدى) قال: إلى الجماع)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r9.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r9.claim: Ibn Qutayba chooses the interpretation that God pairs males and females and guides them to mating.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r10.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r10.claim: Al-Farra explains that God gives each male a female of its kind and inspires the male to approach the mate.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r10.anchor: قال الفراء: (أعطى الذكر من الناس امرأة مثله من صنفه، والشاة شاة، والثور بقرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r11.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r11.claim: Abu Ishaq accepts the mating interpretation because animals mate without having learned it; the broader interpretation of guidance to their welfare also includes this instinct.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r11.anchor: وهذا التفسير جائز؛ لأنا نرى الذكر من الحيوان يأتي الأنثى، ولم يرى ذكرا قد أتى أنثى قبله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r12.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak reads ‘creation’ as created faculties: hands grasp, feet walk, tongues speak, eyes see, and ears hear.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r12.anchor: روي عن الضحاك قول آخر في {أعطى كل شيء خلقه} قال: (يعني اليد: البطش، والرجل: المشي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r13.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r13.claim: On al-Dahhak’s reading, ‘creation’ means what is created: God placed each faculty and its benefit in the relevant bodily organ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r13.anchor: والخلق في هذا القول في معنى المخلوق، والبطش والمشي والنظر وهذه المعاني كلها مخلوق لله تعالى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r14.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r14.claim: Moses’ answer establishes against Pharaoh that creation and guidance require a creator and guide, who is the Lord, and no other lord exists; this supports following God’s religion and guidance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p414/r14.anchor: ثبت خلق وهداية لا خلاف، ولابد لهما من خالق وهاد، ذلك الخالق والهادي هو الرب، لا رب غيره

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:50/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:50/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:50/r1.claim: God perfected each created thing in a form useful to it and most suitable for its purpose, then guided it to its livelihood.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:50/r1.anchor: أتقن كل شيء مما خلق، وخلقه على الهيئة التي بها ينتفع، والتي هي أصلح وأحكم لما يراد منه { ثم هدى } أي: هداه لمعيشته

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r7.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r7.claim: Qatada explains “then guided” as guiding each creature to take what it needs.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r8.claim: Yahya expands this as God directing each creature until it takes what it needs.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r8.anchor: قال يحيى: يقول ثم هداه فدله حتى أخذه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r9.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r9.claim: Mujahid says God fashioned each creature and then taught it what benefits and suits it.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r9.anchor: وقال مجاهد: سوى خلق كل دابة، ثم هداها لما يصلحها وعلمها إياه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r10.speaker: الكلبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r10.claim: Al-Kalbi says God gave each creature its corresponding mate and taught it how to approach its mate.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r10.anchor: وقال الكلبي: أعطاه شكله من نحوه: أعطى الرجل المرأة، والجمل الناقة، والذكر الأنثى، ثم هداه: عرفه كيف يأتيها.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r11.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r11.claim: Al-Hasan cites the verse about God's perfecting all things and asks people to observe how each creature protects itself.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r11.anchor: عن الحسن أنه قال: {صنع الله الذي أتقن كل شيء} [النمل: 88] ثم قال: أم تر إلى كل دابة كيف تتقي على نفسها.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r12.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r12.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r12.claim: Al-Suddi says God gave each thing its fitting form, then inspired it with its livelihood and pasture, according to what it eats.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r12.anchor: وقال السدي: {أعطى كل شيء خلقه} [طه: 50] يعني: صورته التي تصلح له. قال: {ثم هدى} [طه: 50] يعني: ألهمه لمرعاه

TABATABAI:2:21-25#21/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#21/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:21-25#21/r1.claim: God owns all things and may grant others only a dependent permission to act; delegated possession never makes its recipient independent of Him.
TABATABAI:2:21-25#21/r1.anchor: قل اللهم مالك الملك تؤتي الملك من تشآء وتنزع الملك ممن تشآء

BURHAN:v1p104/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p104/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p104/r4.claim: Here هدًى means inspiration or guidance to each creature’s livelihood.
BURHAN:v1p104/r4.anchor: وبمعنى الإلهام ﴿ أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى ﴾ هدى كلا فى معيشته

BURHAN:v4p86/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p86/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p86/r4.claim: The verb “gave” suits things whose existence lasts only one moment.
BURHAN:v4p86/r4.anchor: لان من الأشياء ماله وجود في زمان واحد بلفظ الاعطاء

ITQAN:v2p410/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p410/r16.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p410/r16.claim: In “He gave each thing its form, then guided it,” huda means inspiration about how to secure a livelihood.
ITQAN:v2p410/r16.anchor: 16 والإلهام ﴿ أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى ﴾ أي ألهمهم المعاش

ITQAN:v2p320/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p320/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p320/r6.claim: God gave each thing its created form and guided it to its mate, food, drink, and dwelling.
ITQAN:v2p320/r6.anchor: 1783 ﴿ أعطى كل شيء خلقه ﴾ خلق لكل شيء روحه ثم هداه لمنكحه ومطعمه ومشربه ومسكنه

DAMGHANI:v1p475/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p475/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p475/r3.claim: Hudā can mean inspiration: God inspired each creature how to obtain its livelihood and pasture; 87:3 is grouped with it.
DAMGHANI:v1p475/r3.anchor: الهدى الإلهام قوله سبحانه في سورة طه الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى يعني ثم ألهمه كيف يأتي معيشته ومرعاه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p627/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p627/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p627/r8.claim: Hudā can mean inspiration: creatures are taught their way of life, and the male is inspired to approach the female.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p627/r8.anchor: والثاني عشر : الإلهام . ومنه قوله تعالى في طه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248/r4.claim: God gives each creature its form, including male or female form, then inspires it to approach the female, seek pasture, and avoid dangers.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248/r4.anchor: الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248/r8.claim: The various senses of guidance are related to one another.

JISHUMI:v7p4674/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r7.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r7.claim: Hasan and Qatada say God gave each thing its well-being and guided it toward what benefits it.
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r7.anchor: قيل: أعطى كل شيء صلاحه وهداه لما يصلحه، عن الحسن، وقتادة

JISHUMI:v7p4674/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r8.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r8.claim: Mujahid, Atiyya, and Muqatil say God gave every living thing its allotted form and guided it to food, drink, dwelling, mating, and other needs.
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r8.anchor: وقيل: أعطى كل حي صورته التي قدر له ثم هداه إلى مطعمه ومشربه ومسكنه ومنكحه

JISHUMI:v7p4674/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r9.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r9.claim: Another view says God fitted each thing with its useful limbs: hands for grasping, feet for walking, tongues for speech, eyes for sight, and ears for hearing.
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r9.anchor: وقيل: أعطى كل شيء اليد للبطش، والرجل للمشي، واللسان للمنطق، والعين للبصر

JISHUMI:v7p4674/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r10.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r10.claim: A further view takes khalqahu to mean each creature's kind or form, with each species given its mate and guided to mating.
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r10.anchor: وقيل: أعطى كل شيء خلقه يعني شكله، للإنسان الزوجة، وللبعير الناقة

JISHUMI:v7p4674/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r11.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r11.claim: Abu Ali says God gave creation worldly blessings and guided it to religion, through which the blessings of the afterlife are attained eternally.
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r11.anchor: إلى نعم الآخرة دائما، عن أبي علي. وقيل: أنعم على خلقه

JISHUMI:v7p4674/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r12.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r12.claim: Abu Muslim says God bestowed everything people possess and guided them to their livelihoods and trades.
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r12.anchor: وقيل: أنعم على خلقه بكل شيء يملكونه، وهداه لمعاشهم ومكاسبهم، عن أبي مسلم
